lines.text: One line of SQL made this query over a thousand times faster and it came at a price.
Without an index, the database reads the whole table, a million rows, to find one customer's orders.
With a CREATE INDEX, the query plan switches from SCAN to SEARCH.
The index is a tree sorted by customer, and the search goes straight down to their rows.
Without reading the table, the query dropped from eighty-six milliseconds to five hundredths.
But every new order also goes into the index and writing got thirteen times slower.
Building the index took seven hundred thirty-six milliseconds and almost thirteen megabytes of file.
So it depends on how much the table is read and written. Which column would you index?
